2610.06729.title: Improving Diversity in LLM Short Story Generation
2610.06729.paper_summary: Large language models (LLMs) can generate accurate responses, but these are void of diversity. We attempt to address this for the task of creative short story generation. Drawing on established writing conventions and known LLM limitations, we target variation in genre, tone, style, and named entities. To promote diversity across these dimensions, we introduce DivLM, an LLM post-training framework consisting of two phases. First, we perform continued pre-training on a creative writing corpus and restore instruction-following capabilities using weight residuals. We then apply reinforcement learning with a custom, composite reward function that jointly maximizes diversity across the targeted narrative dimensions while maintaining response quality. Our empirical results on two LLM families show that DivLM increases diversity metrics by more than 9% on average compared to alternative approaches, while preserving instruction following, overall response quality, and similarity to human outputs.
2610.06729.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）可以生成準確的回應，但這些回應缺乏多樣性。我們試圖解決這一問題，針對創意短篇故事生成的任務。基於既定的寫作規範和已知的LLM限制，我們針對類型、語調、風格和命名實體的變化進行研究。為了促進這些維度的多樣性，我們引入了DivLM，一個包含兩個階段的LLM後訓練框架。首先，我們在創意寫作語料庫上進行持續的預訓練，並使用權重殘差恢復指令遵循能力。然後，我們應用強化學習，使用自定義的復合獎勵函數，該函數共同最大化目標敘事維度的多樣性，同時保持回應質量。我們在兩個LLM系列上的實證結果顯示，與其他方法相比，DivLM的多樣性指標平均提高了9%以上，同時保持了指令遵循、整體回應質量和與人類輸出之間的相似性。
